title_en: Supplementary Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Specific Application of Law in Handling Commutation and Parole Cases

articles.content_en: Article 1: For those who refuse to plead guilty and show repentance, or who have the ability to perform but fail to perform or fully perform the property-related judgments in effective judgments, parole shall not be granted, and commutation of punishment shall generally not be granted.

Article 2: For those sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of ten years or more, who meet the conditions for commutation, commutation may be granted only after serving three years; for those sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of less than ten years, who meet the conditions for commutation, commutation may be granted only after serving two years.
If there is a showing of repentance or meritorious service, one commutation shall not exceed six months of fixed-term imprisonment; if there is a showing of repentance and meritorious service, one commutation shall not exceed nine months of fixed-term imprisonment; if there is major meritorious service, one commutation shall not exceed one year of fixed-term imprisonment.
For those sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of ten years or more, there shall be an interval of two years or more between two commutations; for those sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of less than ten years, there shall be an interval of one year and six months or more between two commutations.

Article 3: For those sentenced to life imprisonment, who meet the conditions for commutation, commutation may be granted only after serving four years.
If there is a showing of repentance or meritorious service, the sentence may be reduced to twenty-three years of fixed-term imprisonment; if there is a showing of repentance and meritorious service, the sentence may be reduced to between twenty-two and twenty-three years of fixed-term imprisonment; if there is major meritorious service, the sentence may be reduced to between twenty-one and twenty-two years of fixed-term imprisonment.
When further commutation after life imprisonment is commuted to fixed-term imprisonment, the scope of commutation shall be executed by reference to the provisions of Article 2 of these Provisions. There shall be an interval of two years or more between two commutations.

Article 4: For those sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve, after the sentence is commuted to life imprisonment, if they meet the conditions for commutation, commutation may be granted only after serving four years.
If there is a showing of repentance or meritorious service, the sentence may be reduced to twenty-five years of fixed-term imprisonment; if there is a showing of repentance and meritorious service, the sentence may be reduced to between twenty-four years and six months and twenty-five years of fixed-term imprisonment; if there is major meritorious service, the sentence may be reduced to between twenty-four years and twenty-four years and six months of fixed-term imprisonment.
When further commutation after commutation to fixed-term imprisonment, the scope of commutation shall be executed by reference to the provisions of Article 2 of these Provisions. There shall be an interval of two years or more between two commutations.
Article 5: If a criminal has major meritorious service, the above starting time and interval restrictions shall not apply when granting commutation.
Article 6: When applying parole to criminals of embezzlement and bribery as referred to in these Provisions, strict control shall be exercised.
Article 7: These Provisions shall come into force on June 1, 2019. Where previously issued judicial interpretations are inconsistent with these Provisions, these Provisions shall prevail.
